title: Optimal Division
summary: Given an integer array nums, you can insert any number of parentheses at any position to change the order of operations.
statement: Given an integer array nums, you can insert any number of parentheses at any position to change the order of operations. Your goal is to maximize the value of the expression formed by dividing the elements of the array. Return the expression as a string in its simplest form, without any redundant parentheses.
constraints: Use every number in order with division and return the unique maximum-value expression without redundant parentheses.
hints: Division by a quotient multiplies by its later factors.
Only the first value stays outside; all later values form one denominator chain.
Handle one/two values, otherwise format first/(rest joined by /).
For positive values, moving a later divisor into the denominator increases rather than decreases the result.
editorial: For positive values, moving a later divisor into the denominator increases rather than decreases the result.

tests.explanation: Put every denominator after the first inside one pair: 1000/(100/10/2).
2/(3/4) is larger than every left-associated alternative.
